title: The Williams Correction
title_candidates: Best in Field: The Spoon Gap Blows Out
From Worst to First: Williams at Prince's
theme: Gregg Williams reversed from worst in field (R2, 27 pts) to best in field (R3, 39 pts) at Prince's, while Jon Baker's 28-point day — the round's worst — blew the Wooden Spoon gap from 2 to 13. Mullin survived a front-nine quadruple at H8 by going 10 holes clean on the back nine; Baker's 37 pts (edging Mullin by one) trimmed the Trophy lead from 9 to 8.
opening_hook: Open with the Williams swing — from the field's worst round (R2, 27 pts) to its best (R3, 39 pts) — as the round's sharpest reversal. This sets up the wider theme: Prince's redistributed the misery, and the Wooden Spoon gap was the casualty.
foreshadow: Mullin's quadruple at the par-5 8th leaves him with a front nine to forget — setting up whether he can arrest the damage before the Trophy lead narrows further.

Baker absorbs three consecutive double bogeys at H1-3 and then goes 6 clean holes from H4-9 — planting the possibility that his pattern from R1 and R2 might finally be broken before the par-4 10th intervenes.

competition_state.name: Trophy
competition_state.note: Mullin's lead narrowed from 9 to 8 as Baker edged him by one point (37 vs 36). The Trophy is still Mullin's to lose but Baker gave the closest chase of the TEG so far.

competition_state.name: Green Jacket
competition_state.note: Jacket gap held at 12, but Williams's strong gross round (14 over par, best in field) lifted him above Jon Baker into second — reshuffling the standings without touching Mullin's lead.

competition_state.name: Wooden Spoon
competition_state.note: The Spoon gap exploded from 2 to 13: Williams's 39-point bounce-back and Jon Baker's 28-point worst round of the TEG combined for an 11-point swing. Jon Baker is now firmly isolated in last.

players.arc: Posted 39 Stableford points — best in the field — bouncing back from R2's 27 (worst in field); after a triple at H12 he ran 6 clean holes H13-18 to close, and his Wooden Spoon gap over Jon Baker widened from 2 to 13.
Absorbed a quadruple bogey at the par-5 8th on the front nine, then went 10 holes without dropping a net shot from H9-18 — closing with a birdie at H18 — to post 36 pts and hold his Trophy lead at 8.

Three consecutive double bogeys at H1-3, then 6 clean holes H4-9, then a quadruple at the par-4 10th (one of the hardest, SI3) — yet still posted 37 pts, his best round of the TEG and the only player to outscore Mullin on the day.

28 points — the worst round of the day — including a quad at the par-4 13th (the hardest hole, SI1) and a triple at H17 after three consecutive clean holes; the Wooden Spoon gap over Williams grew from 2 to 13.

venue_notes: Prince's - Shore / Dunes at Sandwich, Kent — TEG's 2nd visit. The Shore and Dunes combination is considered the strongest routing at Prince's. Sitting adjacent to Royal St George's, it is a links of genuine pedigree. Its two hardest holes — H10 (SI3) and H13 (SI1) — both produced quadruples on the day, from Baker and Jon Baker respectively, illustrating what Prince's extracts from any lapse in concentration.

payoffs.payoff: Mullin answered the front-nine damage with a flawless back nine, confirming that the quadruple at H8 was an interruption rather than a collapse.
